alignments.note: Subject and auxiliary ride with the verb (rules 7, 9).
The article follows its noun, so under rule 31 the determiner stays on the noun, supplied there because the noun is anarthrous.

The article governs the expressed head noun ἔθνη and its modifier is a participle, so rule 31's test rather than rule 90's decides: the attributive article realizes nothing and the supplied relativizer is the participle's helper, as τῷ θεῷ τῷ κτίσαντι → *God who created* has it. Reading it as substantival and giving it *who* is what rule 90 forbids, blessing no unit in which a head noun is expressed.

The supplied relativizer *who* is this participle's helper under rules 7 and 31, discontinuously under rule 15; *followed after* is the verb's own phrasal government of an accusative object, which English realizes with no case preposition, so the particle stays inside the unit (rule 106).
Accusative object rendered with *to*: the preposition is the verb's phrasal government and stays with it (rule 106).
Appositional repetition of the noun with the determiner the following article leaves on it (rule 31).
The ASV's appositional *even* answers to this connective particle, which stands unspent, so rule 105's added arm is not reached.
Article following its noun and governing a prepositional phrase keeps only the supplied relativizer (rule 31's carve-out, there being no verb to carry it).
A prepositional phrase has no verb to carry the supplied copula, so *is* goes with the preposition (rules 31, 53).

review_notes: Reconciliation patch: τά becomes unrepresented and *who* moves to διώκοντα, on rule 31's τῷ θεῷ τῷ κτίσαντι → *God who created* and rule 90's own statement that it blesses no unit in which a head noun is expressed.
τήν at the end of the verse is unchanged: its modifier is a prepositional phrase, which has no verb to carry a relativizer, so rule 31's carve-out keeps *which* on the article.
The determiner *the* stays on the anarthrous ἔθνη under rule 31's following-article clause.
A reference comparison will now report τά as a disagreement; that is the convention difference rule 31 requires and not a correction.
